sentences.en: In 1928, a strange phenomenon was sweeping the state of Idaho.
sentences.zh: 1928年，一种奇怪的现象席卷了爱达荷州。

sentences.en: A Boise resident would wake up on a typical Monday morning,
sentences.zh: 博伊西的居民在某个平常的周一早晨醒来，

sentences.en: drag themselves out of bed, get dressed for the day,
sentences.zh: 从床上爬起来，穿好衣服，

sentences.en: and they would hop in their car to drive to work,
not noticing that something was missing.
sentences.zh: 却没注意到少了点什么。

sentences.en: And suddenly, cops in the rear view.
sentences.zh: 突然，后视镜里出现了警察。

sentences.en: Then the next thing that the driver of the car knew,
sentences.zh: 接着，司机还没反应过来，

sentences.en: they were getting picked up because they weren't displaying a license plate.
sentences.zh: 就因为没挂车牌而被拦下了。

sentences.en: Idaho historian Rick Just says license plates?
sentences.zh: 爱达荷州历史学家里克·贾斯特说，车牌？

sentences.en: The Secretary of State was fielding complaints about all the lost tags.
sentences.zh: 州务卿一直在处理关于车牌丢失的投诉。

sentences.en: And soon enough, the culprit became clear.
sentences.zh: 很快，罪魁祸首就浮出水面了。

sentences.en: Tourists would come to Idaho and steal the plates.
sentences.zh: 游客来到爱达荷州，偷走了这些车牌。

sentences.en: Idaho's license plates were being snatched up like plush hotel bathrobes.
sentences.zh: 爱达荷州的车牌就像酒店的毛绒浴袍一样被抢购一空。

sentences.en: People would come up, they would pull up to either a tourist park or a motel or something,
sentences.zh: 人们走过来，把车停在旅游公园、汽车旅馆或其他什么地方，

sentences.en: and they would spot those plates and think, you know, I'd like to have a souvenir.
sentences.zh: 看到那些车牌就会想：嘿，我想要个纪念品。

sentences.en: And so they would just take it off of the car and take it home.
sentences.zh: 于是他们就把车牌从车上拆下来带回家了。

sentences.en: And there was a reason why people couldn't resist swiping Idaho plates in particular.
sentences.zh: 人们对爱达荷州的车牌情有独钟，这其实是有原因的。

sentences.en: That year, the state had revolutionized license plate design.
sentences.zh: 那一年，该州彻底革新了车牌设计。
这是记者丹尼尔·阿克曼。

sentences.en: Before this, plates were basic, with info like the state name and the registration numbers.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，车牌都很基础，上面只有州名和注册号码等信息。

sentences.en: All of this on a pretty simple, solid-colored background.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都印在非常简单的纯色背景上。

sentences.en: But in 1928, the Secretary of State in Idaho had an epiphany.
sentences.zh: 但在1928年，爱达荷州州务卿灵光一现。

sentences.en: He was like, we have this half-square-foot of open real estate just rolling around on everyone's cars.
sentences.zh: 他想，我们每个人的车上都有半平方英尺的空白区域在到处跑。

sentences.en: The 1928 plate is often said to be the very first advertising license plate in the country.
sentences.zh: 1928年的车牌通常被认为是全国第一块广告车牌。

sentences.en: The very first one that tried to advertise a product.
sentences.zh: 第一块试图宣传某种产品的车牌。

sentences.en: And the product that Idaho chose will surprise absolutely no one.
sentences.zh: 而爱达荷州选择的产品，绝对不会让任何人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: The state's 1928 license plates all featured a single, giant potato.
sentences.zh: 该州1928年的所有车牌上都印着一个巨大的土豆。

sentences.en: A big, kind of elongated, goofy-looking potato, but big.
sentences.zh: 一个很大、形状有点长、看起来傻乎乎的土豆，但确实很大。

sentences.en: It was almost as big as the plate.
The registration numbers were stamped in green lettering, right on top of this lumpy, brown spud.
sentences.zh: 注册号码用绿色字体印在这个凹凸不平的棕色土豆上方。

sentences.en: I would say it looks almost fecal in nature.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它看起来甚至有点像粪便。

sentences.en: The execution wasn't perfect, but it was innovative.
sentences.zh: 虽然执行得不够完美，但它很有创意。

sentences.en: Below the tremendous tater, there was even a modest, pragmatic slogan.
sentences.zh: 在这个巨大的土豆下方，甚至还有一句朴实、务实的口号。

sentences.en: Today, every state's got a marketing slogan.
sentences.zh: 如今，每个州都有自己的营销口号。

sentences.en: Missouri is the Show Me State.
sentences.zh: 密苏里是“眼见为实之州”。

sentences.en: But Idaho was the first to put theirs on a license plate.
sentences.zh: 但爱达荷州是第一个把口号印在车牌上的。

sentences.en: They wanted to make sure that when people thought about Idaho, they thought potatoes.
sentences.zh: 他们想确保人们一想到爱达荷州，就会想到土豆。

sentences.en: And for better or worse, the association stuck.
sentences.zh: 不管好坏，这个联想算是扎根了。

sentences.en: And now it's gotten to be such a thing.
sentences.zh: 现在这已经成了一种传统。

sentences.en: I mean, coming up here in a few days at New Year's Eve, we drop a potato.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，再过几天就是新年前夜了，我们要举行“降土豆”仪式。

sentences.en: Well, you know how the Times Square ball comes floating down like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道时代广场的水晶球是怎么缓缓降下的吧。

sentences.en: Well, we have a big potato that comes floating down.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个大土豆会缓缓降下。

sentences.en: They've been doing it about 10 years now.
sentences.zh: 他们已经这么做大约10年了。

sentences.en: The concept of slapping a tagline onto a license plate might not seem like a big deal, but it
sentences.zh: 在车牌上贴标语的概念看起来可能没什么大不了，但

sentences.en: turns out this idea would end up having outsized consequences, and not just for Idaho.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这个想法最终产生了巨大的影响，而且不仅仅是对爱达荷州而言。

sentences.en: We're talking legislative clashes, multiple Supreme Court cases, and even jail time.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是立法冲突、多起最高法院案件，甚至还有牢狱之灾。

sentences.en: Because what started in one state would soon spread.
sentences.zh: 因为在一个州开始的事情很快就会蔓延开来。

sentences.en: And when it did, the question of what should go on a license plate, and what shouldn't,
sentences.zh: 当它蔓延时，关于车牌上应该印什么、不应该印什么的问题，
事实证明，这出奇地具有争议性。

sentences.en: The first state-issued license plates appeared at the very beginning of the 20th century,
sentences.zh: 州政府发放的第一批车牌出现在20世纪初，

sentences.en: and they served a mostly bureaucratic function.
sentences.zh: 它们主要起着官僚管理的作用。

sentences.en: More people were buying and crashing cars every year, so state governments originally
sentences.zh: 每年买车和撞车的人越来越多，所以州政府最初

sentences.en: mandated plates as a way to keep track of all the nuts behind the wheel.
sentences.zh: 强制要求悬挂车牌，以此来追踪那些开车的人。

sentences.en: No one was interested in sloganeering.
sentences.zh: 当时没人对打广告感兴趣。

sentences.en: But then, Americans discovered the road trip.
sentences.zh: 但后来，美国人发现了公路旅行的乐趣。

sentences.en: See the USA in your Chevrolet.

sentences.en: Well, the big factor with increase in automobiles was that it allowed people freedom to roam.
sentences.zh: 汽车普及带来的一个重要因素是，它让人们获得了漫游的自由。

sentences.en: You could go wherever you wanted.
sentences.zh: 你可以去任何你想去的地方。

sentences.en: Christine Byron is a former history librarian at the Grand Rapids Public Library.
sentences.zh: 克里斯汀·拜伦是大急流城公共图书馆的前历史图书管理员。

sentences.en: She focuses on the history of tourism, and she says that the rise of the road trip in the 1920s
sentences.zh: 她专注于旅游史，她说20世纪20年代公路旅行的兴起

sentences.en: created this huge new tourist market.
sentences.zh: 创造了一个巨大的新旅游市场。

sentences.en: Drivers needed services, like gas stations and roadside motels,
sentences.zh: 司机们需要服务，比如加油站和路边汽车旅馆，

When you traveled by steamship or railroad, you pretty much brought what you needed with you,

sentences.en: But once the automobile came along, there was a lot more money that needed to be spent.
sentences.zh: 但汽车出现后，需要花费的地方就多了很多。

sentences.en: From the state's perspective, all those new tourist dollars were up for grabs.
sentences.zh: 从各州的视角来看，所有这些新的旅游资金都等着被赚取。

sentences.en: So states started letting the world know what they had to offer.

sentences.zh: 当时爱达荷人意识到，他们的车牌太珍贵了，不能只印个注册号码。

sentences.en: And Rick Just says once Idaho staked its starchy flag on the license plate, the rush was on.
sentences.zh: 里克·贾斯特说，一旦爱达荷州在车牌上插上了这面“淀粉旗”，热潮就开始了。

sentences.en: License plates became a different thing because of that potato.
sentences.zh: 因为那个土豆，车牌变成了另一种东西。

sentences.en: States spent the middle of the century transforming their plates from austere government documents
sentences.zh: 各州在世纪中叶花费时间，将车牌从严肃的政府文件

sentences.zh: 变成了旅游和工业的彩色宣传品。

sentences.en: You could even think of them as, you know, miniature little ads that are driving,

sentences.en: you know, all over the state and all over the country, hopefully.

sentences.en: In 1940, Arizona stamped Grand Canyon State on its plates and never looked back.
sentences.zh: 1940年，亚利桑那州在车牌上印上了“大峡谷之州”，从此一发不可收拾。

sentences.en: In 1950, Minnesota went with Land of 10,000 Lakes.

sentences.en: Michigan's plate, for example, initially sported the phrase water wonderland in 1954.
